newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bourse seen focused on privatisation units.
newsitem.headline: Polish bourse seen focused on privatisation units.

text.p: Polish shares are expected to extend this week's sideways drift or inch down as mass privatisation NFI units, setting highs in record volumes, are likely to draw most investor attention.

The units jumped six percent this week to 152 zlotys in regular trade and to 153 zlotys in continuous trade in heavy turnovers hitting on Friday all-time record of 106.7 million zlotys on both markets.
The price of the units, distributued to all adult Poles for 20 zlotys apiece, soared 74.7 percent since late August.
The main market's all-share WIG index eased 0.4 percent this week to close at 14,675.9 points and analysts said it expected it to find support at 14,500 or 14,000 points.

"I don't see any chance of a rise and a challenging of the (September 18, 14,832.7-point) main-market high soon, as investors apparently have shifted their attention to the NFI market," said Tomasz Berent of IB Austria Securities.
Some traders saw the units extending gains and stabilising only between 160 zlotys and 200 zlotys.
But analysts said scarce fundamental information about 15 National Investment Funds (NFIs) managing 512 privatised companies, made predicting the unit's performance risky.

Analysts said the recent surge showed many investors believed issue prospectuses of the funds, due to be completed by the end of the year, would prove the units, which are later to be exchanged for shares in the fund, were undervalued.
Analysts said investors would also be watching Monday's food-prices data for September, which would offer clues about the overall consumer prices index, due at mid-month.
Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko said on Friday he estimated year-on-year inflation in September at 18.9 percent, down from 20.5 percent in August.

But analysts said inflation figures were unlikely to move the market as the central bank's Thursday statement that it wanted real interest rates to rise meant a long-hoped rate cut was highly unlikely in the near-term.

Analysts said Thursday's first listing of Paged SA wood and furniture trader on the main floor, would be one of the high points in the otherwise dull week and saw the stock opening well above its issue price of 12 zlotys.
The week's top gainers were Sokolow, which rose 15.7 percent, Rafako 13.3 percent and Polfa Kutno 10 percent.
The biggest losers were PBR which fell 8.6 percent, Stalexport 7.6 percent and Kredyt Bank 6.3 percent.
